data.title: Comparing Two Kinds of River Floods
data.passage: Slow river floods happen after long winter rains fill up every valley. Similarly, melting mountain snow can slowly raise water levels over many days. However, flash floods arrive very fast during a sudden heavy summer storm. Both types of water overflow send water rushing across nearby fields. In contrast, flash floods sweep away cars while slow floods just cover the grass.

structureOptions.label: Compare and Contrast
structureOptions.description: Shows how two things are alike and different

structureOptions.label: Cause and Effect
structureOptions.description: Explains why things happen and what happens next

keyIdeas.text: Winter rains fill up every valley over many days
Arrive very fast during a sudden heavy summer storm
Send water rushing across nearby fields
Sweep away cars and major structures
Just cover the grass without rushing hard

data.authorPurposeExplanation: The author used a compare and contrast structure to help readers understand the important differences between slow and fast river overflows.
